D's Überschrift entspricht der zu V Atr (s. o. S. 167 Sp. 2₃) und ist vielleicht original. Aus G kann In no. Dñi authentisch sein wie in V Atr. Die Agsächs. Worte in G gehören diesem Sammler, denn sie beziehen sich nur auf den kurzen ersten Teil, welchen er kopiert, mit Fortlassung des Restes; s. o. Einl. 1

D’s heading corresponds to that of V Atr (see above p. 167 col. 2₃) and is perhaps original. From G, In no. Dñi may be authentic, as in V Atr. The Anglo-Saxon words in G belong to this compiler, for they refer only to the short first part, which he copies while omitting the rest; see above Introduction 1

Dass D die Zahl zu erfinden ausserstande war, geht daraus hervor, dass er statt MXIIII, welche Zahl vor Wulfstans Predigt steht, MVIIII irrig liest; ed. Napier 156. Vgl. über die Übernahme der Überschrift durch Norwegisches Recht Taranger Angelsaks. Kirk. 258

That D was incapable of inventing the number is evident from the fact that instead of MXIIII, the number that stands before Wulfstan’s homily, he wrongly reads MVIIII; ed. Napier 156. On the adoption of the heading by Norwegian law cf. Taranger Angelsaks. Kirk. 258
Cf. V Atr. G. The heading in G, as Liebermann points out, applies only to the portion of the ordinance reproduced there. As regards the date given in D, cf. Wulfstan, p. 156.

note.label: Christi
note.seg: Be cyricgriðe. In nomine Domini G.

One of the chief features of interest of this code is that it shows how far the Christian conception of kingship had developed. It also shows the respect paid to certain former kings as legislators. It is another of the codes in Archbishop Wulfstan’s style, and, like No. 45, it survives in full only in the C.C.C.C., MS. 201, connected with him. Chaps 1–5.2 survive in another Wulfstan manuscript, B.L.Cott. Nero A. 1. The date is given by the Latin rubric in the Corpus MS. As the code begins “this is one of the ordinances”, and as it is entirely concerned with Church matters, it seems probable that it was once accompanied by a companion ordinance on secular concerns, now lost. The code is edited by Liebermann, I, 263–8; and with English translation by Robertson, pp. 116–29, Thorpe, I, 340–51.

note.label: Christ
note.seg: The rubric is in Latin. The Nero text has instead “Concerning sanctuary”, and, in Latin, “In the name of the Lord.”
